content: 1. Drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 2. Women should be advised to use additional non-hormonal contraception during the first 7 days of therapy. 3. Tablets should be administered in the order directed on the blister pack calendar at the same time each day. 4. Combined hormonal contraceptives increase the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) following delivery. This risk declines rapidly after 21 days but does not return to baseline until 42 days postpartum. 5. According to CDC guidelines, therapy initiation in postpartum women without additional VTE risks should be delayed for 21–42 days. 6. Postpartum women who do not breastfeed or after a second-trimester abortion should wait at least 4 weeks before initiating therapy. 7. Postpartum women who have undergone a cesarean section should wait at least 6 weeks before initiating therapy. 8. Combined hormonal contraceptives, including drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol, should not be used in postpartum women with additional VTE risk factors. 9. Moderate acne in females aged 14 years or older may be treated with oral contraceptives if chosen as a method of birth control. 10. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when coadministered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 12. Ethinyl estradiol coadministered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir can lead to ALT elevations greater than 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), with some cases exceeding 20 times ULN. 13. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and/or dasabuvir. They can be restarted approximately 2 weeks after completing the hepatitis C combination drug regimen. 14. Coadministration of tranexamic acid oral and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Amiloride and drospirenone both increase serum potassium levels, leading to hyperkalemia. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 17. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 18. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 19. Armodafinil decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 20. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when coadministered with ethinyl estradiol. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 21. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol and drospirenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 22. Bosentan decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 23. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for females of childbearing potential. 24. Brigatinib decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 25. Butabarbital decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 26. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of exemestane by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 27. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of fedratinib by other mechanisms. Avoid coadministration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 28. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 29. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the level or effect of drospirenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 30. Fosamprenavir coadministered with ethinyl estradiol may alter hormone levels and decrease amprenavir AUC, potentially leading to loss of virologic response. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 31. Griseofulvin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 32. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 33. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 34. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 35. Leniolisib increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by other mechanisms. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 36. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 37. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 38. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of lonafarnib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for arrhythmias and other cardiac events if coadministration is unavoidable. 39. Lopinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when coadministered with ethinyl estradiol. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 40. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by an unspecified mechanism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration. 41. Mavacamten decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced.
